title: Spain's spy agency warned of Ceuta border breach plans before crisis, declassified files show
description: Spain's national intelligence agency issued multiple warnings about a potential mass crossing of migrants from Morocco into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta, declassified documents show.
fullText:
Madrid — Spain's national intelligence agency issued multiple warnings before the Ceuta border crisis about a potential mass crossing of migrants from Morocco into the Spanish exclave in late July, according to declassified documents released by the government on Wednesday.

The trove of 40 documents, which includes alerts, intelligence reports, charts and communications from multiple law enforcement and intelligence agencies, appears to undermine what Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has said about the level of warning the government had before the sudden influx took place.

There have been major protests in Spain in response to the migrant arrivals, with critics blaming the Sánchez government for its handling of the crisis, and his political opponents accusing him of pandering to Morocco.

On July 29, a day before more than 72,000 people began pouring into the Spanish city neighboring Morocco, Spain's spy agency, the National Intelligence Center (CNI), sent an alert via WhatsApp to the Spanish government's delegation in Ceuta about calls on social media "for an assault on the fence and by sea tomorrow at 8 p.m."

"There are two different groups with a total of 180,000 followers," the declassified WhatsApp message from the intelligence agency said, "just to give you an idea of its scale."

A report from Spain's spy agency sent that day to Moroccan intelligence services warned of plans on social media for migrants to enter Ceuta on July 30 by climbing a border fence separating the exclave from Morocco, or by swimming around it, the documents show. It mentioned that migrants might take advantage of Morocco's national Throne Day, celebrated on July 30.

That same day, Spain's national intelligence agency issued similar warnings about "several groups on Facebook and WhatsApp encouraging these attempts" in messages to Spain's Civil Guard police force.

Once thousands of people were streaming across the border on July 30, a Defense Ministry intelligence report issued that day stated that Moroccan forces were passive and acted negligently to stop migrants.

"It cannot be ruled out that Morocco may attempt to exploit the situation that has arisen in Ceuta to further its strategic interests," the report went on.

Morocco's foreign ministry didn't immediately respond to a request for comment from The Associated Press about the documents.

On Wednesday, Sánchez rejected the idea that the declassified documents revealed that there was prior warning about a border crisis of the scale that took place between July 30 and 31.

"The existence of this campaign was known ... and was being monitored, but in no way did it constitute or could it be interpreted as an indicator of the scale, nature, or probability of what happened afterward," Sánchez wrote on X, referencing the spy agency's July 29 warning about what was brewing on social media.

Sánchez has defended his government's handling of the crisis and said last week there was no evidence that Morocco's government orchestrated the incident. That sparked further criticism, particularly after a leaked police report alleged the involvement of Moroccan police in the episode.

Several weeks after the initial border rush, Ceuta is dealing with a prolonged humanitarian crisis because of some 5,000 migrants who remain in the small city, according to the national government. Local officials cite a higher figure of up to 10,000 people.

They include unaccompanied minors, the Reuters news agency notes, adding migrants are living in makeshift camps or on Ceuta's streets and beaches, according to local authorities.

The Spanish leader pledged last week to release documents related to Spain's deadliest mass crossing, in which NGOs reported that more than 140 migrants died.

In the days immediately before the mass crossing, hundreds of migrants had swum from Morocco to reach Ceuta, which Spain's Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska acknowledged at the time.

He said authorities were facing "an extraordinary, exceptional situation," and that the Spanish government was "dealing with it with the means that we already have deployed there permanently."

Wednesday's document trove includes reports from multiple agencies that detailed the increasing number of arrivals, a surge that overwhelmed authorities beginning July 30.

title: Iran likely to reverse-engineer captured US underwater drone
description: Iran's capture of a U.S. military underwater drone gives Tehran an opportunity to study and potentially reverse engineer the vessel,
fullText:
WASHINGTON, Sept 9 (Reuters) - Iran's capture of a U.S. military underwater drone gives Tehran an opportunity to study and potentially reverse engineer the vessel, delivering a setback for the Pentagon and drone maker Anduril.

The U.S. military and Anduril have downplayed ‌the significance of the drone falling into Iranian hands. The vessel, a Dive-LD autonomous underwater vehicle designed for long-range surveillance and other ‌undersea missions, is among a new generation of military drones intended to operate for days with little human intervention. Washington has previously treated the loss of advanced drones to Iran as a ​serious matter.

After Iran captured an RQ-170 Sentinel stealth reconnaissance drone in 2011, then-President Barack Obama publicly asked Tehran to return the aircraft. Iran later claimed it had reverse-engineered the drone and subsequently unveiled domestically produced models that appeared to draw heavily on its design.

More recently, the U.S. military moved swiftly to prevent Iranian forces from taking possession of uncrewed maritime technology. In 2022, a U.S. Navy patrol ship and MH-60S Seahawk helicopter were deployed after an Iranian naval vessel attempted to tow away ‌a Saildrone surface vessel in the Gulf, according to ⁠the Navy.

Analysts say Iran is unlikely to gain a decisive military advantage from the captured drone, but the episode nonetheless represents a propaganda victory for Tehran and an awkward setback for Washington's efforts to project technological superiority.

Iranian embassies ⁠around the world have mocked the U.S. for losing its drone. Iran's embassy in Ghana, in a post on X, boasted about picking the submersible up in "a strait controlled by people who can hear a shrimp sneeze," adding that, "Our guys picked it up like a plastic bottle in a fishing net. Fully intact. Still blinking like an ​idiot. ​Condolences to whoever was holding the joystick."

U.S. Navy Captain Tim Hawkins of U.S. Central Command ​said the "defective drone was an older model that neither collected ‌sensitive data nor carried any classified sonar or radar equipment." Anduril did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

"Of course Iran will take every opportunity as a propaganda win," said Farzin Nadimi, a senior fellow at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy. "It can help the (Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps) make better versions of their own designs."

Iran will almost certainly try to pry open the drone's hardware, but the drone's software carries built-in defenses, said Bryan Clark, a senior fellow and director of the Center for Defense Concepts and Technology at the Hudson Institute. Iranian engineers "could definitely reverse-engineer the mechanical systems," he said, pointing to ‌Tehran's track record with captured American aircraft.

"Unboxing ceremony by our reverse engineers, tomorrow morning!" Iran's ​embassy in Hyderabad wrote on X.

The incident has also highlighted a disconnect between the messaging ​of Anduril and its customer, the U.S. Navy.

Navy officials said the Dive-LD was ​an older-model vehicle that suffered a malfunction and was recovered by Iranian forces after being left "dead in the water."

Anduril has promoted ‌the Dive-LD as "the most reliable and flexible" large autonomous underwater vehicle ​available, saying it is capable of ​operating for up to 10 days in demanding conditions. In addition to its use by the U.S. Navy, the Dive-LD was the testbed vehicle for the development of Australia's new Ghost Shark large underwater drone.

"This is something that Iran has proven very adept at exploiting for its own ​benefit in terms of seeking to frame the narrative ‌as one of U.S., in this case, ineptitude and their ability to sort of retain control over the Strait of Hormuz," said ​Mona Yacoubian, director of the Middle East program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

title: Talarico says he 'missed the mark' as he backtracks on controversial woke statements
description: James Talarico now backs banning transgender surgeries for minors and opposing trans athletes in girls' sports as the Texas Senate race heats up.
fullText:
In a Fox News exclusive interview, Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico came out in favor of banning gender surgery for minors and opposed transgender-identifying men competing in women's sports.

Talarico also backtracked on several of his more controversial claims, including saying there are six genders and that "God is nonbinary."

This comes as the Texas Senate race, which is surprisingly close according to recent Fox News polling, enters its final months. The race is considered critical to both parties' chances of securing a Senate majority. Talarico is facing Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, a Republican who has faced controversies of his own. A Republican loss in Texas would significantly impact President Donald Trump's ability to implement his agenda.

Fox News spoke with Talarico at a food drive campaign event in Dallas on Tuesday. Talarico's event took place as the first-ever GOP midterm convention kicked off just miles away in downtown Dallas.

Talarico Campaigns With Surgeon Who Operated On Transgender Minors: 'Wolf In Sheep's Clothing'

Asked whether he would vote as a U.S. senator in favor of a national ban on gender surgery for minors, Talarico answered, "Absolutely."

He said, "I've been consistent on this issue," explaining his opposition to a Texas bill to ban transgender surgeries on minors by saying the measure "was overly broad."

"If you go back and check, I voted for a major amendment to limit the bill to banning surgeries for minors," he said. "As a lawmaker, my job is to try to sift through everything the bill does. And sometimes there's stuff in it that's really harmful, and I have no choice but to oppose the bill as a whole."

"It's why I try to use amendments, to narrow the focus of the bill so that it does exactly what we intend it to do," he continued. "It's what I tried to do with that piece of legislation, and unfortunately, the amendment I supported was unsuccessful."

In 2023, as a member of the Texas House of Representatives, Talarico voted against a state bill titled SB 14, which prohibited certain gender surgery, puberty blockers and certain hormone treatments for minors. There were 18 amendments to the bill proposed by Democrats, all of which Talarico voted in favor and all of which ultimately failed.

In the same interview, Talarico acknowledged that men in women's sports is a significant issue in Texas. He said, "I oppose trans athletes playing in girls' sports if it endangers safety or fairness."

"Every sport has to be safe and fair. As a former public school teacher, I care a lot about our student athletes. I care a lot about our students. And so, I will oppose trans athletes playing in girls' sports if it risks safety or fairness," he said.

Talarico's comments mark a shift from his earlier position as a Texas state lawmaker.

In 2021, while serving on the Texas House Public Education Committee, he opposed SB 29, which sought to require public-school athletes to compete based on the biological sex listed on their birth certificate, calling the issue a "manufactured problem." Later that year, he voted against HB 25, which enacted similar restrictions into Texas law.

James Talarico Admits Past Comments 'Missed The Mark' When Confronted On Claims Like God Is 'Non-binary'

He also addressed perhaps his most controversial statement, which he made in 2021, while opposing a Texas bill to keep men out of women's sports. Talarico said on the state House floor that "God is both masculine and feminine and everything in between. God is non-binary."

"I was being provocative with that statement. I get that," Talarico admitted, explaining, "What I was trying to say is that you can't use human categories to define God, and that's not controversial theologically. In fact, the late Charlie Kirk, the late Pope Benedict all said the same thing."

Talarico continued, claiming "these comments are being clipped out of context to try to distract from Ken Paxton's career of corruption."

"You mentioned [Paxton] being acquitted in the state Senate. That was after two of his billionaire megadonors gave the lieutenant governor a $3 million check to buy his acquittal," Talarico said. "So, Ken Paxton is the most corrupt politician in Texas, and he's gonna try to clip some of my comments, including comments where I was being a little provocative in order to try to distract from that career."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Paxton campaign for a response.

Longtime Gop Aide Defects To Dem Rising Star As Texas Senate Battle For Cornyn's Seat Heats Up

Regarding his past comment about there being more than two genders, Talarico said he does not currently believe there are six sexes.

"I've missed the mark on some of my past statements. I will be the first to admit it," he said. "What I meant is that there are two sexes, and then there's a small percentage of people with genetic abnormalities."

"Obviously didn't say it correctly. There are not six sexes. There are two, and I think the reason that politicians in that convention center across the street want to talk about six sexes is because they don't want to talk about $6 diesel," he said.

Though he walked back these controversies, Talarico did not hold back on his criticism of the Supreme Court, which he described as "infected" with corruption, saying it "needs to be overhauled."

He said that if elected, "You're going to expect that I will vote for overhaul to the Supreme Court. That will include binding codes of conduct for our justices. It'll include term limits, and I am open to a discussion about expanding the number of justices."

Following these controversies, Talarico pledged to keep his message focused on affordability for the remainder of the campaign.

"Everywhere I go across the state of Texas, people are struggling to survive in this economy. They are struggling to afford the basics: groceries, gas, utilities, healthcare. And that's what I'm going to be focused on from now until Election Day."

On the topic of affordability, Talarico said that "we should not have a state income tax" in Texas. This is despite Talarico previously voting against a measure to permanently ban a state income tax, which he suggested was redundant and an example of "government waste at its worst."

The measure was ultimately passed by the Texas Legislature and approved by Texas voters in November 2019.

title: NATO aircraft deployed in Poland as Russian jet-powered drones strike Ukraine
description: Russia and Ukraine exchanged hundreds of strike drones overnight.
fullText:
NATO "military aviation" assets were deployed in Polish airspace overnight, according to the Armed Forces Operational Command in Warsaw, in response to Russian jet-powered drone attacks on targets in western Ukraine.

The command said in posts to X that it conducted "a short-term elevation of readiness of selected forces and assets" in response to the attacks. "The actions were of a preventive nature and were aimed at ensuring the safety of Polish airspace, particularly in areas adjacent to those affected by Russian strikes," it added.

The command said in a subsequent post to X that "military aviation continues to operate, and ground-based air defense and radar reconnaissance systems remain in an appropriate state of readiness" in response to what it called "the emergence of further potential threats to the security of Polish airspace." The operations concluded after around two hours.

Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 149 drones into the country overnight, with the craft used a mix of Shahed strike drones -- around half of which were jet-powered -- and Gerbera and Parody decoy drones. Ukrainian defenses downed 128 drones, the air force said, with impacts reported across 13 locations.

'Complex' Russian attacks kill 5 in Kyiv after US peace talks visit, officials say

Ukraine's State Emergency Service reported impacts on a residential building in Kyiv and attacks in the Dnipropetrovsk region, in which at least eight people were injured.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said in a post to Telegram that at least three people were injured when a drone hit a gas station in the capital's Holosiivskyi district.

In the northeastern city of Sumy, meanwhile, at least two people were killed and 23 others injured in a strike on a shopping mall, local officials said.

Russia's Defense Ministry said that the southern Ukrainian city of Mykolaiv and the southwestern city of Chornomorsk were among the targets of its overnight strikes. The ministry also said it targeted two dry cargo ships that were heading to the Ukrainian Black Sea port city of Odesa.

The Defense Ministry in Moscow also said its forces downed at least 448 Ukrainian drones overnight. The craft were intercepted above 13 Russian regions, plus occupied Crimea, the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea, the ministry said.

Russia's escalating strikes in Ukraine increasingly spilling into NATO, Romania says

From Wednesday evening through Thursday morning, Russia's federal air transport agency -- Rosaviatsiya -- reported temporary flight restrictions at airports in Sochi, Tambov, Penza, Saratov, Volgograd, Krasnodar, Grozny, Vladikavkaz and Makhachkala.

Rosaviatsiya also announced temporary restrictions at Vnukovo and Domodedovo international airports in Moscow.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a post to Telegram on Thursday morning that Kyiv's forces attacked "eight Russian infrastructure targets that support the war effort" over the previous 24 hours.

Among them were a refinery in the Yamalo-Nenets region and a maritime trading port in Dagestan, Zelenskyy said, as were unspecified targets in Moscow, Voronezh, Astrakhan and Bryansk. "Russia continues its daily terror against Ukraine, and it receives a just response every day," he wrote.

description: Bone fragments from the sword hand of a medieval Russian prince who won a famous victory over the Mongols have been sent to the front in Ukraine to raise
fullText:
MOSCOW, Sept 10 (Reuters) - Bone fragments from the sword hand of a medieval Russian prince who won a famous victory over the Mongols have been sent to the front in Ukraine to raise army morale in the Russian Orthodox Church's latest show of support for President ‌Vladimir Putin's war.

The sarcophagus of Grand Prince Dmitry Donskoy, who died in 1389 and is revered by Russian nationalists for defeating the Mongol Golden Horde at ‌the 1380 Battle of Kulikovo, was uncovered this summer during restoration work at Moscow's Cathedral of the Archangel inside the Kremlin.

Putin personally inspected what experts said were the prince's well-preserved remains in August, hailing them ​as "an absolutely unique and marvellous discovery" which reinforced the foundations of Russian history.

The Russian Orthodox Church, which has backed Putin throughout the conflict, said it had dispatched a fragment of Donskoy's right hand to Donetsk, one of four Ukrainian regions Putin said he had incorporated into Russia in 2022, a move Kyiv rejected as an illegal land grab.

Referring to Donskoy as "the holy commander," the Moscow Patriarchate of the Russian Orthodox Church said part of his remains had been sent to the front to stand invisibly shoulder-to-shoulder with Russian troops.

"A fragment of the ‌Grand Prince's right hand – the very same right hand with ⁠which he wielded his sword on Kulikovo Field – has been sent to the front to strengthen the soldiers' spirits," it said in a statement.

The relic, held in a small ornate casket beneath toughened glass, will be shown to Russian combat units along the more than 1,000-km ⁠front line, it said.

Donskoy, whose name was given to a Soviet tank column funded by the church in World War Two, was declared a saint by the Russian Orthodox Church in 1988.

The carefully choreographed effort to use his remains in a public relations exercise to boost patriotism and morale comes ahead of a parliamentary election later this month.

Russian military and church officials have ​presented ​the discovery as a fortuitous find that could help Russian forces prevail in Ukraine, now in ​the fifth year of a grinding war.

The tour also comes as ‌Russian forces seek full control of the Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine and as diplomatic efforts to end the war have yet to yield a breakthrough.

Donskoy's relics were carried through the streets of Moscow at the weekend in a huge Orthodox procession.

At a ceremony at a World War Two memorial in Donetsk on Tuesday, Sergei Kiriyenko, Putin's first deputy Kremlin chief of staff, joined military commanders and the Russian-installed regional head in kissing the relic and making the sign of the cross as a priest read a prayer.

"Both our military personnel and the people who live in Donbas need strengthening from above, need God's help and the blessing of our saints," Metropolitan Vladimir of Donetsk and Mariupol, a senior Moscow-appointed ‌cleric, said. Donbas is a broader area incorporating Donetsk and neighbouring Luhansk which Russia controls almost in ​its entirety.

Elsewhere, commanders have presented Donskoy's remains as evidence that God is on Russia's side.

The Defence Ministry ​on Wednesday released footage of troops in the Sverdlovsk region attending a church ​service carrying icons and Orthodox flags, alongside an interview with a commander who said the relics would support Russia's victory.

Critics, however, have accused ‌the Church of breaking with religious protocol to please the Kremlin. ​They have also questioned why Donskoy's remains, whose ​location was broadly known for decades, were recovered and venerated only now, 38 years after he was declared a saint.

"By the fifth year of war, the Church leadership in Moscow began to wonder what else it could do to show its support for what Russia terms its 'special military operation'," Alexander Zanemonets, an ​Orthodox priest and historian based outside Russia, wrote in a note ‌for the Carnegie Russia Eurasia Center whose director Russia has designated a "foreign agent."

"It had already sent priests to the front lines, instituted mandatory prayers ​for Russian victory in every church, and flown icons over cities. A state embroiled in war will try to compel all institutions, including religious ​ones, to participate in it."

title: Analysis-Fearless US stock market vulnerable to shocks as midterms loom
description: With two months until the U.S. midterm elections, the options market is showing a potentially toxic mix of fragility and fearlessness, with some
fullText:
NEW YORK, Sept 9 (Reuters) - With two months until the U.S. midterm elections, the options market is showing a potentially toxic mix of fragility and fearlessness, with some analysts worried markets are ill-prepared to absorb any shock.

Despite recent bond market volatility, stocks remain near record highs, volatility ‌measures are near 2026 lows, and equity market correlations are flirting with record lows, meaning stocks are moving more independently than usual.

While analysts do not expect the ‌elections themselves to prompt a big market reaction, the run-up to the November 3 vote could be volatile.

As the elections approach, investor focus could turn to the uncertainty over control of Congress and its policy implications — along ​with the risk of a divided or fragile government — which could stir volatility, analysts said.

Historically, the September-October lead-up to the midterms has been a volatile period for equities as markets exit the typically quiet summer months and investors zero in on political risk.

The S&P 500 has dropped 5% or more during the September to October period in 15 of the 24 midterm years since 1930, according to a Cantor Fitzgerald analysis.

But you wouldn't know that from looking at volatility futures.

The options-based investor anxiety gauge, the Cboe Volatility Index, recently touched a new low for the ‌year. At around 15, it is below its long-term median ⁠of 17.6. VIX futures also look calm, as investors remain confident strong corporate earnings will continue to support markets.

"The VIX curve is not expressing any premium for midterm elections," said Michael Purves, CEO of Tallbacken Capital Advisors.

A plethora of potential catalysts — including data on inflation and jobs, a ⁠Federal Reserve meeting, and a late-September U.S. visit by Chinese President Xi Jinping — fill the calendar over the next two months, culminating in the midterms.

The elections themselves have market implications, some analysts said. The Democratic Party has gained a significant edge over Republicans in voter perceptions of which party has a better approach to the cost of living, a troubling sign for President Donald Trump's party, a ​Reuters/Ipsos ​poll found.

Should Democrats wrest control of the House of Representatives, the shift from one-party control of the ​White House and both chambers of Congress could add uncertainty to ‌markets, Julian Emanuel, lead equity and quantitative strategist at Evercore ISI, said in a note.

"A Senate flip would magnify the dynamic," Emanuel said.

title: UConn women's basketball staff visits Class of 2027 No. 2 recruit Ivanna Wilson Manyacka
description: UConn will host four top-10 Class of 2027 recruits for official visits, including the top two in the class.
fullText:
UConn women's basketball is about two months out from the start of the season. Preseason practices begin in the next few weeks, yet Geno Auriemma remains busy with his summer recruiting efforts.

The Huskies remain in the running for four top-10 recruits in the Class of 2027. All four have their official visits to Storrs scheduled for the coming months, while one received a home visit from the Husky staff this week.

Ivanna Wilson Manyacka, the No. 2-ranked recruit in the class, posted a picture of her posing alongside Auriemma and UConn assistant coaches Morgan Valley and Nykesha Sales on her Instagram story Wednesday morning. The Maryland native posted the picture with the caption: "I appreciate you guys for coming on a home visit!!"

From her Instagram, looks like UConn women's basketball coaches Geno Auriemma, Morgan Valley and Nykesha Sales took a home visit to Ivanna Wilson Manyacka (the No. 2-ranked recruit in the Class of 2027) this week pic.twitter.com/0L0hyeFfdT

Manyacka recently took an official visit to LSU. ESPN reported in August that she's also expected to take official visits to Notre Dame, Duke, Texas, North Carolina, UCLA, Maryland, and UConn. Her visit to Storrs is expected to be in November.

The 6-foot-2 guard spent the summer helping lead Team USA to gold in the Under-17 FIBA World Cup. She was named the MVP of the tournament after averaging 12.9 points and 1.7 assists per game.

Fellow Class of 2027 guard Sydney Savoury told ESPN on Wednesday that her official visit to Storrs will be on Oct. 23 - two days before the Huskies' Oct. 25 exhibition against Army. Savoury is the No. 9-ranked recruit in the group and is down to her final six schools: UConn, USC, Texas, North Carolina, UCLA and Notre Dame. ESPN reported that she's already visited USC and UNC.

title: Tech Alums Set to Dominate NFL Week 1 With Historic Australia Debut
description: Keion White leads 11 Georgia Tech former players into NFL Week 1. See the full schedule, stats, and why the ProJackets are ready to play.
fullText:
Georgia Tech former players are flooding the NFL slate for Week 1, led by Keion White's historic Thursday night kickoff in Australia. Eleven Yellow Jackets are set to play across the league, with four rookies making their first NFL appearance. This isn't just a busy weekend; it is a full-scale takeover of the gridiron by Tech alumni.

Keion White will be the first #ProJacket to take the field when his 49ers face the Los Angeles Rams. The game happens Thursday at 8:35 pm on Netflix, marking a massive global moment for the program. White enters his 49ers tenure as a key piece of the defensive line. His presence in Melbourne sets the tone for a weekend where Tech talent is everywhere. According to Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets, this debut is a unique opportunity to showcase local grit on a world stage.

The rest of the group follows with a packed Sunday schedule. Zeek Biggers, in his second NFL season, plays for the Miami Dolphins against the Las Vegas Raiders. FOX will broadcast the match on Sunday, Sept. 13 at 4:25 pm. Biggers brings defensive depth to Miami that Tech fans know well. Jordan Mason, a veteran in his fifth season, runs for the Minnesota Vikings against the Green Bay Packers. His Week 1 stats show 17 yards on just 3 rushes in the preseason, proving he is ready to grind.

Four rookies are set to make their NFL debuts this Sunday, and the data suggests they are ready to contribute immediately. Haynes King, a quarterback for the Carolina Panthers, faces the Chicago Bears at 1:00 pm on FOX. His preseason stats are impressive: 21-for-34 passing for 180 yards, 2 touchdowns, and 39 rushing yards with 1 rushing score. Keylan Rutledge, an offensive lineman for the Houston Texans, also faces his first real test against the Buffalo Bills. For his Week 2 showing versus the Raiders, NFL.com assigned an "A" grade to Keion White. That is a rare early accolade for a first-year player.

Other key names include Rodney Shelley for the Los Angeles Chargers and Jackson Hawes for the Buffalo Bills. Shelley faces the Arizona Cardinals at 4:25 pm on CBS with 9 tackles and 3 passes defended in the preseason. Hawes, in his second season, plays at the Houston Texans at 1:00 pm on CBS. He recorded 2 catches for 8 yards in 2 preseason games. Meanwhile, veterans like Harrison Butker and EJ Jenkins anchor their teams. Butker, in his 10th season, kicks for the Kansas City Chiefs against the Denver Broncos on Monday, Sept. 14. He hit a 69-yard field goal in preseason, showing he still has a cannon. EJ Jenkins, in his fourth season, plays for the Philadelphia Eagles against the Washington Commanders at 4:25 pm on FOX. He posted 20 yards on 2 catches in 3 preseason games.

The sheer volume of Tech players on the field proves the program's development pipeline is working at an elite level. Having 11 former players active is a statistical anomaly that demands attention. The mix of rookies like Haynes King and veterans like Harrison Butker shows a complete range of talent. According to Yahoo Sports, the focus remains on how these players handle the pressure of opening week. The data from the preseason is clear: they are not just making the roster; they are making an impact.

From the 69-yard kick by Butker to the "A" grade for Rutledge, the numbers tell a story of readiness. The schedule is tight, with games starting as early as 1:00 pm and running late into Monday night. This concentration of talent means every Tech fan has a reason to watch Sunday. The 2026 preseason stats confirm that these players have earned their spots through hard work. The 17 rushing yards by Mason and the 180 passing yards by King are just the beginning. This weekend belongs to the Yellow Jackets.

title: Zay Flowers, Devontez Walker pop up on Ravens’ 1st 2026 injury report
description: The Ravens released their first injury report of the 2026 regular season.
fullText:
The Baltimore Ravens are starting the 2026 season in relatively good health.

Cornerback Bilhal Kone and running back Adam Randall, the team's injured reserve placements during roster cuts, are more like stashes who were not expected to contribute early in the year, if at all. Losing Danny Pinter, who was leading the starting center competition, is certainly a blow, but he was no guarantee to win the job, either. And on the first injury report of the regular season, only four players are listed, all with limited participation.

Linebacker Teddye Buchanan (knee) and defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) are still ramping up from the injuries that ended their 2025 season. Playing in Week 1 seems to be within reach, though the team may want them to put in at least one full practice on either Thursday or Friday.

Wide receivers Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Devontez Walker (groin) were both listed as limited, though Flowers said after practice that he expects to play on Sunday in Indianapolis. An absence from Walker would give sole possession of the WR3 role to third-round pick Ja'Kobi Lane. Fourth-rounder Elijah Sarratt would also take on a game day role.

The Colts also reported four players as limited, including two starters: wide receiver Alec Pierce (heel) and safety A.J. Haulcy (ankle). Pierce missed all of training camp as he recovered from offseason ankle surgery. He is expected to play against the Ravens, but may do so on a pitch count as he ramps up to 100%. Haulcy, a third-round pick, is listed as the team's starting strong safety; 2025 seventh-rounder Hunter Wohler would be in line to start if the rookie cannot go.

Indianapolis' other injuries are to backup center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger (illness) and No. 3 blocking tight end Drew Ogletree (neck). Offensive lineman Josh Sills and tight end Pharaoh Brown would likely be elevated from the practice squad as replacements.

title: Connecticut athletic leaders see no need to separate public, private schools in state tournaments
description: Debate has resurfaced in neighboring states. There no plans to change in Connecticut.
fullText:
With the CIAC football season kicking off this week, a familiar debate is percolating in some nearby states: Should public and private schools compete in the same postseason tournaments?

According to some league commissioners, the answer, at least for Connecticut, is a resounding no.

"I don't think the answer is segregating them to their own particular league or tournament," said Jim Buonocore, Ledyard's athletic director and the commissioner of the ECC. "I think our state needs to do a better job in terms of how we classify those schools for the postseason. I think we've gotten to that point in basketball. With the success multiplier, things have opened up on the boys and girls side where it's more balanced, but I don't think that formula is at 100% of my approval but it certainly answered some of the questions."

The possibility of changes in Pennsylvania and New York has once again pushed the question to the surface.

In April, the Pennsylvania House of Representatives overwhelmingly approved a bill which would allow the state's governing body, the PIAA, to separate public and private schools for their playoffs.

In New York, Section 1, which includes Westchester, Rockland, Duchess and Putnam counties, voted 69-4 to amend their local constitution and bar private schools from competing against public schools in its postseason tournaments. A New York State Public High School Athletic Association appeals panel responded by overturning the amendment, putting on hold a change which was slated to take place for the 2027-28 season.

In both states, schools were classified as boundary schools, public schools which are limited to one town or area, and non-boundary schools, which can draw students from anywhere.

The issue has in the past been a hot topic among fans of Connecticut athletics, but CIAC executive director Glenn Lungarini said there have been no formal proposals during recent years.

"I think in most of our team sports, the success factors that are used have really pushed teams that are successful on a more frequent basis up to those higher divisions," Lungarini said. "Another challenge in Connecticut, is there's so few Catholic schools that honestly, it'd be really hard to run a tournament with just those schools."

Gregg Simon, CIAC associate executive director, said any changes would have to come from the membership, meaning schools and principals, and go through the CIAC Board of Control.

"With the small number of private schools that we have in Connecticut, it would obviously be very difficult to be able to have a division solely of private schools. The cases (in Pennsylvania and New York), you have much larger states and many more schools. You may have the opportunity if their membership chooses to do so, to create a separate division."

Connecticut has 15 Catholic schools within the CIAC. Three are all-girls schools and another, Kolbe Cathedral, do not have a football team. Among the others, three are part of co-ops: Immaculate with Abbott Tech; St. Paul with Avon; and St. Bernard with Montville.

Of the 11 teams playing football last year, only four, Fairfield Prep, Holy Cross, Northwest Catholic and St. Joseph, qualified for the CIAC tournament.

Another barrier to separate divisions is the overall picture of many sports, not just football.

Buonocore was the chairman of the CIAC football committee when the coaches committee in 2008 proposed that technical schools and cooperative schools have their own division.

"We had four divisions at the time and we proposed a fifth division with the tech schools and co-ops and let them have their own state championship," Buonocore said. 'That's what those schools and coaches wanted and we were representing the coaches on that committee as part of the CHSCA. The feedback we got then was that we can't create a separate division because that would be something they'd have to do across the board."

The issue tends to arise when private schools experience success, especially when its prolonged winning.

In hockey, Notre Dame-West Haven and Fairfield Prep combined to win five straight Division I titles from 2018 to 2024 before Darien and New Canaan won the last two seasons.

In basketball, West Haven's boys championship headlined a season in which no private school won a state title in CIAC boys and girls basketball. Prior to that, a private school had won at least one state title every year since 2017 in girls basketball and since 2014 in boys basketball.

The obvious factor being, non-boundary schools aren't experiencing overwhelming success, despite the ability to bring in new players.

"It happens in baseball, in Class S where you have a Catholic school, a school without borders, winning and that's where the cry comes from," SCC commissioner Al Carbone said. "You see it in some girls sports as well. But I don't see that happening just yet because for one thing it's a small state and there are only a few Catholic schools."

Carbone also pointed out the disparity in success among the Catholic schools and even across different sports at the same schools. St. Paul, for example, has won two straight Class S championships in baseball, but co-ops with Avon in football.

"Unless you're going to do multipliers for every sport, which I think is probably the best solution, you've got to be consistent in every sport," Carbone said. "It's not like in other states where (private) schools are playing national schedules. It's a totally different environment in Connecticut."

title: ESPN College GameDay is no longer appropriate for children, some parents say
description: Pat McAfee received criticism for cussing and encouraging fans to do so ahead of the LSU vs. Clemson game.
fullText:
ESPN College GameDay returned this past weekend to preview Week 1 of the college football season, including LSU's matchup against Clemson.

The three-hour show, which first aired in 1987, continues to be a popular way for college football fans to begin their Saturdays.

However, some believe ESPN star Pat McAfee is making the show no longer appropriate for kids.

McAfee encouraged LSU fans to sing "Neck" on multiple occasions Saturday morning. The song includes the lyrics "Suck that Tiger [expletive], [expletive]."

Some fans took to X and complained that they no longer feel like they can watch the show with their kids.

"Hey @CollegeGameDay can you tell Pat McAfee to watch his mouth? I could watch College Gameday with my kids until he came on. We just turned it off because he can't control his tongue… @espn @ESPNCFB @Disney," one post said.

Another added: "Honestly, I am just sick of hearing 'suck that Tiger [expletive] [expletive]' on a dang morning show. We all know they say it but why do we need to have it blasting at 10:45 am on national TV? My kids love watching College Gameday but man I hate that part every year when they're in BR."

As the show was kicking off, College GameDay posted a video of McAfee on X.

In the 32-second video, McAfee said, "Hello beautiful people. After a long, long offseason, College GameDay is all the way back from Baton Rouge, baby. ... It's hot as hell, the storylines are in abundance, and college football's about to showcase to the world why it's the greatest sport on earth. We start here at 9 a.m. Eastern on ESPN. ... Let's go."

The comments section was filled with complaints about McAfee and what the show has become.

"Impossible watch. Thank you for ruining something great," one fan said.

Another fan said, "Yeah, he's the reason that, after 28 years of Gameday being must see tv for me 3 hours every Saturday morning, I don't tune in anymore. His schtick was funny for about 10 minutes then it just got old."

McAfee clearly has a large following and is one of the biggest personalities in sports media.

The complaints, however, suggest a segment of the college football audience has grown frustrated with his presence on the show.

title: River Ryan debuts in Mud Hens victory
description: Scores, news, and notes, from around the Tigers’ farm system for Wednesday, September 9, 2026.
fullText:
River Ryan's debut in the Tigers organization went well, and the Hens won pretty comfortably on Wednesday.

Ryan is working back from a right hamstring injury that he aggravated in trying to return with the Dodgers too soon. So the Tigers have understandably taken their sweet time getting him back on the mound. He only went two innings this one, but he proved the stuff is as electric as ever. He allowed two soft hits, at least one of which should have been an out, and struck out two without a walk. The fastball topped out at 98.2 mph and averaged 97.1, and Ryan mixed in all six of his pitches during the outing.

The Hens started to build a lead in the top of the second. Corey Julks led off with a walk but was caught stealing. Seby Zavala singled, and after James Outman struck out, Justice Bigbie singled as well. Veteran catcher Carlos Pérez stepped in and cracked a three-run shot to left for a 3-0 lead.

In the fourth, Outman led off with a walk and Pérez came through again with an RBI double to make it 4-0.

Carl Edwards Jr. took over from Ryan in the bottom of the third. He cruised through his first three innings, striking out the side swining in the fifth.

In the sixth, Outman doubled and Bigbie singled him to third. A Pérez double play ball got the run home for a 5-0 lead.

Finally in the bottom half, Edwards faltered a bit, allowing two run, but he pitched into the seventh with no more issues. Ty Madden got the final out in the seventh.

Outman singled in Julks in the top of the eighth, stole second base, and scored on a Bigbie single to make it 7-2.

Madden handled the eighth, and Nic Sandlin tossed a scoreless ninth to wrap it up.

Outman: 2-3, 3 R, RBI, 2B, BB, K, SB

Ryan: 2.0 IP, 0 R, 2 H, 0 BB, 2 K

Edwards Jr. (W, 6-10): 4.2 IP, 2 ER, 4 H, BB, 5 K

Coming Up Next: It's a 7:38 p.m. ET start on Thursday.

Lucas Ellisalt was knocked around in this one, and the SeaWolves bullpen struggled even more as the Phils crushed them on Wednesday.

Things got off to a promising start in the top of the second as E.J. Exposito singled and then rode home on a Chris Meyers blast to left center field. 2-0 Erie.

Chris Meyers lofts a 2-run homer to left center to give Erie an early lead. pic.twitter.com/huhqX7SvVk

Elissalt was cruising early on, but started to struggle to get ahead of hitters and paid for it. He gave up a run in the third, and walked two batters after that before managing to escape an further damge. He wouldn't be so lucky in the fourth. He fell behind Aroon Escobar and came back with a 3-1 fastball that got launched for a solo shot. Another solo shot off a hanging slider in the inning made it a 3-2 Reading lead and they wouldn't look back.

Elissalt gave up two singles and a walk to start the fifth, and that was it as Colin Fields took over. He allowed two of those runners to score, and it was 5-2 Reading.

Fields got into trouble of his own in the sixth, and Yoniel Curet took over only to surrender a three-run shot and then a solo homer.

A solo shot from Thayron Liranzo was the only bright spot the rest of the way as the Fightin Phils contined to add on.

Rough night for Erie, but Thayron Liranzo gets them slightly closer with a solo homer to right center. It’s his 17th home run of the year. pic.twitter.com/4dvocPxw0C

Elissalt (L, 0-2): 4.0 IP, 5 ER, 6 H, 3 BB, 3 K

title: Titans scouting report vs New York Jets: Matchups, edges, our score prediction
description: With the New York Jets coming to town to start Robert Saleh's tenure as Tennessee Titans coach, it's easy to get caught up in the past. Let's serve the present.
fullText:
The only thing that no one's going to talk about as the Tennessee Titans prepare for their season opener against the New York Jets is the game itself.

The Titans host the Jets to start the 2026 NFL season at Nissan Stadium on Sept. 13 (noon CT, CBS). All the scuttlebutt about Titans coach Robert Saleh's past life coaching the Jets and the fleet of former Jets he signed to rebuild the Titans roster and the smaller fleet of former Titans who've ended up playing for the Jets and the broad, general misery that these two fanbases have endured in the last few seasons figures to overshadow the game itself which, by all accounts, should be one of the week's least compelling.

The Jets and Titans come into the year tied for the third-worst odds to win the Super Bowl per BetMGM. Jets QB Geno Smith feels like an obvious stopgap. Titans QB Cam Ward has massive expectations he needs to start living up to. Jets coach Aaron Glenn might already be on the hot seat. And Saleh's got to prove his poor results with the Jets weren't because of bad philosophy, but because of a bad situation.

Still, there's plenty of talent on both sides of the ball, and more than a few matchups worth watching.

The Jets' secondary famously didn't intercept a pass in 2025, so more than a little bit of work went into revamping it. In one offseason, the Jets added veteran Nahshon Wright, Minkah Fitzpatrick and Dane Belton and second-round pick D'Angelo Ponds. Combine those additions with edge defenders David Onyemata and David Bailey, the No. 2 pick in the draft, and the Jets have a new arsenal of weapons to prevent passing success.

So, obviously, do the Titans in the inverse. Ward adds Wan'Dale Robinson as a go-to slot option and third-down specialist and No. 4 draft pick Carnell Tate as his deep threat, intermediate target and red zone favorite. Throw in Calvin Ridley's return from injury and there's a good argument that Ward will be throwing to three receivers who are all more talented than what his best options were at the end of last season.

This matchup of revamped weakness turned potential strengths might be the story of the game. Whoever more successfully installs their new toys takes a huge advantage.

KEEP READING: For his next trick, Brian Daboll aims at Cam Ward and improving Titans | Exclusive

The Jets have early-round pedigree just about everywhere on offense. Receiver Garrett Wilson and running back Breece Hall are studs. Tackles Olu Fashanu and Armand Membou are developing nicely. Rookies Kenyon Sadiq and Omar Cooper Jr., are extra toys to use on the perimeter. There's a lot of talent here, even if there are questions about Smith's viability as a starting-caliber quarterback.

That ability to attack the Titans on the outside might be an advantage, especially with the criticisms defensive backs like Alontae Taylor, Cor'Dale Flott, Amani Hooker and Kevin Winston Jr., drew throughout training camp. But the Titans also have the advantage up the middle, with defensive linemen Jeffery Simmons and John Franklin-Myers representing a best-case scenario for how to attack an offense through the A and B gaps.

Saleh's defense is about attack mentality and going full speed instead of reacting to keys. If Simmons and Franklin-Myers are successful enough getting off the ball that the Jets can't get the ball to the perimeter, consider the Jets' strengths neutralized. If not, well, the Titans begin at a disadvantage.

The uncomfortable reality is that the Jets might be the more talented team overall. But they're in a messier spot than even the Titans, and the Titans' greatest strengths are a little more developed and easier to deploy. Saleh's defense carries the way in this one.

Nick Suss is the Titans beat writer for The Tennessean. Contact Nick at nsuss@gannett.com. Follow Nick on X @nicksuss.

title: Benn does not deserve world title shot - Garcia
description: Ryan Garcia says Conor Benn is nothing more than an "average fighter" and does not deserve a shot at his WBC welterweight title.
fullText:
Ryan Garcia says Conor Benn is nothing more than an "average fighter" and that the Briton does not deserve a shot at his WBC welterweight title.

Garcia, 28, makes the first defence of his belt against Benn at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on Saturday.

The American has consistently dismissed Benn's ability during the build-up and, after skipping Tuesday's face-off, has been accused overlooking the 29-year-old.

But Garcia says he is not taking anything lightly as he aims for a 26th win in 29 bouts as a professional.

Asked whether Benn, who has not fought at welterweight since April 2022, deserves the opportunity to challenge for a world title, Garcia said: "Not at all."

He told BBC Sport: "He's an average fighter, he's athletic and it's his last name. It's not a shot at him; it's just the bitter truth.

"I'm preparing like he's the best fighter in the world. It's all about preparation and how sharp you are.

"People could say you're overlooking him. No, I'm calling it how I see it.

"Do you want me to say he's as good as Floyd Mayweather? He's not.

"He's alright. He comes forward and throws looping overhands. He's aggressive and will make him a rugged fight, but it's not something I haven't seen before."

Garcia and Benn have documented their fight camps on social media, but have presented their preparations in different ways.

Benn has posted videos of his training regime, while Garcia has been collaborating with influencers and making appearances in the WWE.

"He's not my cup of tea. I wouldn't want to hang out with him too much," Garcia said.

"He's a bit of a hypocrite and contradicts himself a lot. I am who I am - goofy and outgoing, making jokes and having fun.

"He is trying to say he's humble, but he's out here any chance in a Rolls Royce. He loves the lights.

"He thinks I'm like that, but I'm focused on my craft 100%."

title: Five things Wisconsin Badgers fans must know about Western Illinois
description: The Wisconsin Badgers are just days away from what seems to be a very winnable game against Western Illinois.
fullText:
The Wisconsin Badgers are just days away from what seems to be a very winnable game against Western Illinois.

The Leathernecks come into this one 1-1, having defeated Northwestern (IA) 65-14 in Week 0, and then falling to Illinois State 41-10 in Week 1.

Wisconsin is 0-1 after a dreadful second-half performance resulted in Notre Dame blowing them out, 41-13.

With all eyes on the Badgers' home opener, here are five things UW fans need to know about the Western Illinois Leathernecks.

It seems to be a quarterback by committee, as both Carson Carsell and Kennedy McGill have seen significant playing time in both games.

Caswell is 14/26 for 164 yards with no touchdowns and one interception, while McGill is 29/39 for 317 yards with two touchdowns and one interception.

McGill had 15 carries for 98 yards with three rushing touchdowns in Week 0, which officially gave him a five-touchdown game. The senior had a much tougher time on the ground in Week 1 with 12 carries for just 18 yards.

The 6-foot-1 senior wideout has nine receptions for 166 yards, which leads the team by a wide margin. For reference, no other receiver has more than 100 yards; the next closest is Jacob Kania's 63, and 44 of those came on one reception.

The Iowa native started the year with a bang as he had a sack and a forced fumble, and then he led the way with nine tackles against Illinois State, and also added another sack.

Another Midwesterner has made a mark on this team, as Buckner is a sophomore and an Illinois native who comes into Week 2 with an impressive 13 tackles, 10 of which are solo, along with a sack against Illinois State.

title: Why Giants can beat the Cowboys in Week 1: Scouting report, prediction
description: See our prediction, scouting report and key matchups for Giants vs Cowboys in Week 1 season opener.
fullText:
Here's a closer look at the Giants' season opener against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, Sept. 13:

Sunday, 8:20 p.m., MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford, New Jersey

John Harbaugh was 7-1 in home openers in Baltimore, and now he brings that record with him to the Meadowlands. The Giants will be physical and the floor for the entire team has been raised with the way Harbaugh has prepped them for this season. Can they match the Cowboys offensively and do enough in stopping Javonte Williams to unleash this pass rush and finally make Prescott uncomfortable. Maybe even a late game catch from Odell Beckham Jr. in his Giants' return, and Harbaugh's team gets a much-needed win.

Cowboys' keys to victory: Dak Prescott has owned the Giants since his rookie season when he lost twice to Ben McAdoo's Big Blue team in 2016. His weapons, George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb, have a chance to overwhelm every defense in the NFL. How improved is this defense with Rashan Gary, Quinnen Williams up front and rookie Caleb Downs out to prove the Giants – and everyone else – should not have passed on him?

Giants' keys to victory: Jaxson Dart went through the wringer early in training camp in a new offense and against this defense, but he has been on his game over the past two weeks, showing the Giants' staff that he's starting to get it again. He needs to show he can win from the pocket and excel at the routine plays in addition to the spectacular. Malik Nabers is the biggest difference maker on the roster.

Giants OLB Abdul Carter vs. Cowboys LT Tyler Guyton. Carter is poised for a breakout season in Year 2, and he was strong down the stretch of his rookie season with 4.5 sacks in the final five games. The Cowboys say they have complete confidence in Guyton, but he's going to have his hands full. The Giants have to put heat on Prescott from jump.

title: No 'surprise' about Sabah's progress
description: Journalist Katie Wilson, who covers football in Azerbaijan, joined BBC Radio Manchester's Michael Clarke and Wes Brown on Total Sport to give an insight into Thursday's Champions League opponents Sabah.  Wilson said the club's progress should not come as a surprise, despite their relative lack of experience.  "The club is only nine years old, they had to go through four qualifying rounds," she explained.
fullText:
Journalist Katie Wilson, who covers football in Azerbaijan, joined BBC Radio Manchester's Michael Clarke and Wes Brown on Total Sport to give an insight into Thursday's Champions League opponents Sabah.

Wilson said the club's progress should not come as a surprise, despite their relative lack of experience.

"The club is only nine years old, they had to go through four qualifying rounds," she explained.

"I think in Azerbaijan it's not such a surprise, this was always the intention when the club was launched. It was always the intention to compete in Europe."

Asked whether there would be a big gulf in quality, Wilson said Sabah would be determined to make an impact after navigating four qualifying rounds.

"You don't go through four qualifying rounds to just be happy to be there. I think they really will want to get some points. I think being from a smaller association where people don't know too much about them could actually be an opportunity to make the most of that.

"People won't know their style, and if we look at how they fared in the qualifying rounds, sometimes they went in as the underdog but were able to overturn it.

"Maybe if United have control of the game and get comfortable, that's when Sabah could be quite dangerous."

Wilson also revealed an unusual detail about Sabah manager Valdas Dambrauskas, who funded his coaching education after appearing on a TV gameshow.

She explained: "Dambrauskas didn't have a professional playing career but he did go on 'Who Wants To Be A Millionaire?' in Lithuania when he was 25-years-old, I believe. He won 4,000 litas, which is around £1,000. He used that to fund his coaching course in the UK."

title: Why TC Taylor said Jackson State football can score 80 points in a game
description: Jackson State football coach T.C. Taylor explains what he's most impressed with about his team's play through two games.
fullText:
After surviving a scare at Tennessee State and cruising past Edward Waters, Jackson State football gets to experience its first off week undefeated, as planned.

The Tigers (2-0) will take the weekend off before hosting Division II Tuskegee (1-1) at Mississippi Veterans Memorial Stadium on Sept. 19 (6 p.m. CT, SWAC TV).

"Going into the bye week right where we want to be, 2-0," coach T.C. Taylor said at his weekly press conference on Sept. 8. "We talked about it as a program, so this week is just about the execution and getting better, working on the little things and continue to build and get better for Tuskegee next week."

The week off gives Taylor and his staff an early opportunity to evaluate the team and outline points of emphasis.

The Tigers' offense is coming off a high-powered performance in which it totaled 704 yards of offense and scored 66 points. Taylor is particularly pleased with the number of players who showed they can rotate in and out at each position.

"If we can get 60, we can get 80," Taylor said. "… I've been saying all along, the talent we have this year offensively, we just haven't had that depth like that in a while. … So many other guys were able to come in and step up. … Each and every week, you never know what they're capable of. The sky's the limit with that group when you've got that kind of talent on the offensive side of the football."

Taylor noted that similar depth exists on the defensive side of the ball, but he was more complimentary of the defense's ability to apply corrections in subsequent weeks.

Ahead of the game against EWU, Taylor emphasized the importance of getting off the field on third down. JSU improved from allowing TSU to convert 12 of 19 third downs to allowing EWU to convert just 4 of 14.

"They're doing what we're asking them to do," Taylor said. "We talk about improving on the third down stuff, they go out there and really take it upon themselves to try to get better. Then I told them we've got to find ways to get to the quarterback. We got to the quarterback. So just each and every week, they're building."

Although the Tigers are playing well, Taylor knows they're not perfect. Through two games, penalties have been a consistent issue. Against TSU, JSU committed seven for 53 yards. Against EWU, the Tigers had nine for 89 yards.

Taylor pointed out a difference between judgment calls for holding penalties and "boneheaded" penalties like unsportsmanlike conduct, acknowledging that he's more focused on cutting down on the latter.

"The ones that I cannot tolerate is the unsportsmanlike, false starts and things like that," Taylor said. "Those are the ones that we're going to address. … It's something we're going to continue to emphasize, especially when we get close to conference play, because those could be a problem for us."

title: Oilers’ Connor McDavid sees ‘positive’ signs ahead of 2026-27 NHL season
description: Connor McDavid says Edmonton must go through every regular-season checkpoint.
fullText:
Connor McDavid sees encouraging signs around the Edmonton Oilers ahead of the 2026-27 NHL season. Speaking Wednesday after an informal skate at Downtown Community Arena, McDavid praised the team's early energy.

"Yeah, it's been good," McDavid said. "I've liked what I've seen. Guys came in early and guys are ready to go. There's lots of energy in the room, which is great."

He then gave his personal assessment, saying, "All signs are positive."

MORE: NHL's decentralized draft decision draws strong backlash from analysts

The optimism comes after Edmonton endured a disappointing 2025-26 campaign. The Oilers finished 41-30-11 with 93 points, despite scoring 282 goals.

Edmonton ranked sixth in NHL scoring and led the league on the power play. However, the Oilers allowed 265 goals, ranking 25th across the league.

The team's defensive issues eventually contributed to a first-round playoff exit. Edmonton lost its series against Anaheim 4-2 after entering the postseason with championship expectations.

Anaheim, California, USA; Edmonton Oilers center Connor McDavid (second from left) celebrates with teammates at Honda Center. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

McDavid thinks that last season taught Edmonton an important lesson about maintaining standards throughout the regular season.

"I don't want to say we took it for granted or complacency," McDavid said. He pointed to consecutive Stanley Cup Final appearances as a possible factor.

"You go to a Cup Final two years in a row," McDavid said. "You feel pretty good about your group and when it matters, you're going to turn it on."

He admitted that approach cannot work consistently in today's NHL. "The league's too good," McDavid said. "Teams are too good to not kind of go through the checkpoints."

That message fits Edmonton's current situation, with the roster seeking more consistency around its elite core. The Oilers must improve their defensive structure while maintaining their offensive strength.

MORE: Oilers' Connor McDavid reveals why he loves playing in Montreal

McDavid also emphasized urgency during the team's early preparations. "Guys are already digging in hard and getting ready for camp," he said.

"We want to hit the ground running this year."

For an NHL contender like the Oilers, that mindset matters. Edmonton cannot rely solely on McDavid and Leon Draisaitl to rescue inconsistent performances. A stronger team structure could determine whether these early positive signs translate into another deep playoff run.

title: Arch Manning failed against Ohio State last season. He can flip the script in Round 2
description: Arch Manning didn't live up to the hype against Ohio State last season. He has a chance to flip the narrative in round two of the series on Sept. 12.
fullText:
Arch Manning doesn't like re-watching the game film from Texas' loss to Ohio State last season.

"It's rough film to watch," the second-year Texas starting quarterback told reporters Monday, Sept. 7. "I don't like watching it that much."

REQUIRED READING: Save your Arch Manning hot takes. Judgement day looms for Texas football

The fourth-year quarterback is a different player than he was in Week 1 of 2025, his first game as the Longhorns' full-time starter. The Manning-led Texas offense scored only seven points in the 14-7 loss on the road last season, with Manning completing 17-of-30 passes for 170 yards with a touchdown to an interception.

When No. 3 Texas hosts No. 1 Ohio State in a rematch of last season's game, Manning has the opportunity to show how much he has improved in the time since.

"Feel like I'm a year better," Manning said. "Anytime you go throughout a season, get reps, get game experience, then a whole offseason to get better and a game last week, feel like I'm a year better."

The heralded former five-star recruit and latest quarterback from the Manning family entered the 2025 season with huge — sometimes unfair — expectations. The outside frustrations regarding his play hit a high note in Week 3 against UTEP, when he completed only 11-of-25 passes for 114 yards with a touchdown to an interception, leading an offense that scored 27 points against one of the worst teams in FBS.

Manning flipped a switch down the stretch last season, though, starting to fulfill those expectations. He scored 19 of his 36 total touchdowns in Texas' last six games, throwing for 300 or more yards in three of those final matchups.

He wasn't the only quarterback that looked like a different player throughout the 2025 season. Heisman Trophy finalist Julian Sayin also made his first start as the full-time starter against Texas last season, and he completed 13-of-20 passes for a measly 126 yards with a touchdown in the win before going on to have one of the best seasons among quarterbacks in college football.

Texas coach Steve Sarkisian is expecting a vastly different game with both quarterbacks in different parts of their careers.

"Pretty drastically different," he said of the two quarterbacks. "I just think you see the level of confidence that both guys are playing with. I think what you notice is the presence in the pocket. I think you notice their confidence to use their legs, you saw Julian do it last week. He tucked it and ran for a touchdown.

"I just think the confidence. Both guys deliver the ball with accuracy, you see the trust and timing. Pretty drastic difference of the two players now the second time around going up against one another. So should be pretty high-level quarterback play come Saturday."

Manning looked comfortable in Texas' Week 1 blowout of Texas State, completing 20-of-27 passes for 305 yards with four touchdowns in the 59-7 win, albeit with an interception. The additions of Auburn transfer Cam Coleman and a new-look running game led by Hollywood Smothers and Raleek Brown only helps Manning's case.

The spotlight will be on the second-year starter in Week 2, especially with ESPN's "College GameDay" in town for the game. There are expectations, too, for Sarkisian, who's 0-2 against Ohio State the last two seasons, including in the College Football Playoff semifinals.

Manning is embracing the challenge.

"This is why you come to Texas, to play in these big-time games," he said. "Excited it's at home against a really good team and a good defense. We're excited. I'm going to take it all in, but live in the moment right now."

With a Heisman matchup against Sayin and fellow contender Jeremiah Smith, along with CFP implications on the line, Manning has a chance to flip the script on his doubters.

It would certainly cool off the bad film he put out a year ago.

"Not a lot of good memories a year ago," Manning said. "Hoping to have a good game this year."
